item.content:encoded:
I've already upvoted, as I think the attention to rhythm, rhyme and throwing in all the classic elements of the site is perfect -J material. The line that clinched it for me was the "Serpent's Hand" reference.

I would however second the request to fix the lines above.

+ Suggestions within
- Better off without

To put it most politely, it's a putrid world-eatingdevouring beast!

The whole world would be blown apart from London to Daytona Beach!

Though hell if we won't try, 'cause we're the netherworld'smultiverse's constable

You could use "netherverse's" too, I guess. I also really don't understand the "class a day with X and K" line.

There are some lines that could be strengthened - those around the "Torture Town" bit feel a little like padding. If you could put in references to titanium, reality bending and/or SCP-2000 instead, I would give you a second upvote.1

One other nitpick. "Dispense" is obviously to distribute, but "Dispense with" means stop using. Therefore I think that "Dispense all the amnestics" would be a better start to the second-last line.

Footnotes
1. Seriously, I would find a way.

item.content:encoded:
I love it. I always love a well-done Major General parody, and this rhymes and scans almost perfectly. I found a few lines that have one too few syllables, so I'm presenting them for your consideration:

+ show block
– hide block

To put it most politely, it's a putrid world-eating beast! — unless you pronounce "world" with two syllables, this needs tweaking to flow properly
(It's best say "900-J" so names can never trouble you) — you probably missed "to" after "best"
In short, a hostile monster that class a day with X and K! — something feels missing between "that" and "class", cause the sentence doesn't really make sense
The world would be blown apart from London to Daytona Beach! — best place for a syllable would be between the first two words if possible (or change them to one that scans)
Though hell if we won't try, 'cause we're the netherworld's constable, — best place for a syllable would be between the last two words if possible (or change them to one that scans)
